articles.headline: Eagles release wide receiver Hollywood Brown per request
articles.description: Receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Eagles upon his request.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルス、ハリウッド・ブラウンWRを本人の希望で解雇
articles.descriptionJa: シーズン前半にわずかな出場機会にとどまっていたWRのハリウッド・ブラウンが、本人の希望によりイーグルスから解雇された。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Wide receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday upon his request.

The two sides came to terms on a noninjury settlement that will offer financial relief to Philadelphia as part of the agreement, a source told ESPN. The Eagles are comfortable moving on from Brown with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due to soon return from injuries, and with Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon emerging as solid options.

Brown, 29, signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. He was brought in along with Wicks, Elijah Moore and Lemon to help complement Smith following the trade of A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots.

A significant role for Brown never materialized, however, even with injuries to Smith and Wicks. He appeared in four games (one start) and had five catches for 63 yards on eight targets. All five of his catches resulted in first downs.

Brown acknowledged he anticipated playing more when he joined the team but said he wasn't taking anything personally.

"I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said in October as questions swirled about whether he'd be traded before the Nov. 10 deadline.

"It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for.

"Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play," he added, "but at the end of the day, it's not my plan."

Brown has played for the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs, Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens over his eight-year career. He had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Chiefs in 2025.

articles.description: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: 【情報】ペリカンズのマレーがトレードを希望、双方が解決に向けて協議中
articles.descriptionJa: ペリカンズのガード、デジョンテ・マレーがチームからのトレードを希望している。ESPNのシャムス・チャラニア記者への情報によると、代理人のクリッチ・スポーツCEOリッチ・ポールとチーム関係者が解決に向けた話し合いを開始した。
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Murray has made it clear to the organization that he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere, according to sources.

The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Murray has been ruled out because of a left ankle sprain for Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Memphis Grizzlies.

After the latest game, Murray tweeted a response to an account that noted that the Pelicans are 3-0 without Murray in the lineup and 1-8 with him on the court: "From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!," the since-deleted tweet read.

Murray, 30, was acquired by the Pelicans in a June 2024 trade with the Atlanta Hawks, as New Orleans dealt two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels, Larry Nance Jr. and E.J. Liddell to Atlanta for him. Murray was coming off a 2023-24 season in which he averaged 22.5 points, 6.4 assists and 5.3 rebounds per game.

He has dealt with major injuries and played just 54 games over the past three seasons, however. He has averaged 16.6 points, 6.6 assists and 5.9 rebounds for the Pelicans, shooting just 41.9% from the floor. He broke a hand in the 2024 season opener and suffered a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon in January 2025. Murray is averaging just 13.4 points per game this season.

Murray, who made the All-Star team in 2022, is making $32.8 million this season and has a player option for $30.8 million next season.

articles.body:
The NBA's leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Offseason buzz

ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal!

Nov. 13

Murray, Pelicans working toward trade

New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania.

Murray has made it clear he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.

From Bobby Marks: Murray signed a four-year $114 million extension with Atlanta in July 2023 but was traded the following offseason to New Orleans. He has two years remaining on his contract -- $32.8 and $30.8 million, respectively, with a player option in the second year.

One salary-cap nugget a team interested in Murray will have to consider is the $2.4 million in unlikely bonuses. While he did not reach any of the incentives in the previous season, unlikely bonuses are applied to the first and second apron. With Murray on their books, New Orleans is $4 million below the luxury tax and $5.7 million under the first apron hard cap.

Despite five players (including the $44.9 million nonguaranteed contract of Zion Williamson) earning more than $21 million in 2027-28, New Orleans is well positioned below the luxury tax and apron.

After not having a first-round pick in the 2026 draft, New Orleans could have two picks in the top four in 2027 -- its own and Milwaukee's. If one of those picks falls between Nos. 5 and 30, the least favorable would go to Atlanta.

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to discuss the NBA's mounting injury problem, including how Stephen Curry's recent injury will impact the Golden State Warriors' hot start. They move on to the injuries of Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves for the Los Angeles Lakers before covering Caleb Wilson's broken hand in Chicago. They close with the Cleveland Cavaliers' big response after a slow start and the Minnesota Timberwolves' impressive play without Anthony Edwards.

articles.headline: Prosecutors: Text shows Rozier, friend planned to bet unders on Hornets teammate
articles.description: A co-defendant in an NBA betting case told a gambler that he and Terry Rozier were planning a wagering scheme centered on another Hornets player, federal prosecutors alleged in a court filing.
articles.headlineJa: 検察：メッセージで判明、ロージエと友人がホーネッツのチームメイトに「アンダー」で賭ける計画を立てていた
articles.descriptionJa: NBAの賭博事件の共同被告が、テリー・ロージエと共に別のホーネッツ選手を対象とした賭博スキームを計画していたことをギャンブラーに伝えていたと、連邦検察が法廷提出書類で主張した。
articles.body:
A co-defendant in an NBA betting case told a gambler that he and Terry Rozier were planning to bet unders on the statistics of another Charlotte Hornets player, federal prosecutors alleged in a court filing Friday.

In April 2023, Deniro Laster allegedly texted co-conspirator Marves Fairley that he and Rozier were "setting up another under bets, this one involving one of Rozier's then-teammates," prosecutors wrote in the filing. It is unclear whether Rozier knew about Laster's text. It is also unclear whether the teammate, who was not named, was aware of any plan or whether any attempt to bet on his unders took place.

The text message was allegedly sent about two weeks after Rozier left a March 23, 2023, game between the Hornets and New Orleans Pelicans in the first quarter. Rozier allegedly agreed to a $100,000 bribe to leave the game early and benefit bettors who wagered on the under on his statistics. Fairley, a Mississippi bettor, pleaded guilty to felony charges in the case and admitted in court that he had agreed to pay an NBA player to manipulate his performance.

The government alleges in the filing that Laster messaged a different then-NBA player he knew in April 2023 and asked if they were "tryna make 100k gang." The NBA player was not named.

"It is our understanding that no other NBA player other than Terry Rozier is alleged to have engaged in any misconduct related to the gambling scheme claimed to have been perpetrated by Rozier and Deniro Laster," an NBA spokesperson told ESPN in a statement. "We continue to cooperate with the government's investigation."

David Markus, Rozier's attorney, told ESPN on Friday that they deny the new allegations "in the strongest possible way."

"Terry Rozier is innocent," Markus wrote in a court filing Thursday. "The objective evidence proves it. Unlike every other individual charged in this sweeping conspiracy, he never placed a bet on an NBA game or player prop, and he had no knowledge that anyone else was betting on his performance."

Rozier and Laster have pleaded not guilty to charges related to sports bribery, honest services, wire fraud and money laundering. 

An attorney for Laster did not immediately respond to a message left by ESPN.

The government has not charged Laster or Rozier in relation to the alleged plan involving the Hornets teammate. A spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York declined to comment.

In the filing, the government also accused Rozier of lying to the NBA during the league's investigation and failing to turn over all his phones. They asked the judge to admit into evidence that Rozier is paying for the legal defense of Laster and his siblings.

"The NBA's investigation into Rozier's conduct in connection with the March 23 Game remains open, and the NBA has not cleared Rozier," the filing states.

Friday's government filing alleges that Rozier told people close to him that the March 23 game would be his last of the season. Rozier

articles.body:
United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, while Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their list, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. It was announced on Friday that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

articles.headline: Fantasy hoops managers are giving up on Mikal Bridges, here's why you shouldn't
articles.description: Andre explains why Mikal Bridges continues to hold fantasy value despite the poor start to his season.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーバスケのオーナーたちがミカル・ブリッジズに見切りをつけ始めているが、諦めるべきではない理由
articles.descriptionJa: シーズン序盤の不調にもかかわらず、なぜミカル・ブリッジズがファンタジーでの価値を持ち続けているのか、アンドレが解説する。
articles.body:
Mikal Bridges is off to an objectively bad start to the season from a fantasy basketball perspective. Bad enough that I've been called out on social media for having him so high in my early season rankings.

Through his first 10 games this season, Bridges averaged 6.3 PPG and 0.9 3PG on 32.9 FG%. His cold shooting is affecting his minutes, leading New York Knicks coach Mike Brown to sit Bridges in the fourth quarter and therefore limit him to only playing 25.1 MPG. His peripheral stats like rebounds, assists, steals and blocks are actually right on his norms on a per-minute basis, but his reduced minutes have led to lower totals there as well.

Production-wise, this was Bridges' worst 10-game regular season stretch since March of this year, when he averaged 8.4 PPG and 1.0 3PG on 35.5 FG%. In fact, extended cold scoring spells aren't unusual for Bridges if you look at his career. Sometimes his shot just won't go in. But when the slump is over, Bridges has always returned to his typical high-level self. Last season, that 10-game stretch was swallowed by his other 72 games. All told, Bridges averaged 14.4 PPG on 49.0 FG% for the season that, along with his other stats, led to him finishing top 30 in the league in fantasy points as well as in the ESPN Player Rater.

And that's the point.

While Bridges' shot can be inconsistent, his production over the long haul is metronomic. He plays every game ... period. He has played in all 648 games in his nine-year career, never missing a single game. In the 2022-23 season Bridges was traded in the middle of the campaign, so he actually played 83 regular season games that year. But in an NBA full of injuries and load management, Bridges' iron-man durability is a super power.

Another of his fantasy super powers is the versatility of his game. Bridges is a 3-and-D player who contributes a bit to every category. Those contributions add up in both category leagues and points leagues, to the point that he always ends up among the top 30 in fantasy production. And the consistency has been across roles and teams, as well. In his last four full seasons leading up to this one, he split a season between being a role player for the Phoenix Suns and the primary scorer for the Brooklyn Nets in 2022-23, was a primary scorer for the Nets (23-24), and then was back to a role player with the Knicks since 2024-25 -- and his fantasy points (both totals and per game) end up roughly the same every year.

He always ends up at the same spot.

Always?

Bridges' incredibly slow start this season rightfully raises some questions. After having him in my preseason top-40 fantasy rankings, Bridges has slid outside the top 80 in this week's rankings update. The rankings factor in feedback from the current season, and Bridges' fantasy average is just far below his norm.

But, again, a closer look shows that only one aspect of Bridges' game is out of whack right now: his shooting, which is directly affecting his scoring and minutes played.

articles.headline: NFL Week 10 uniforms: Titans debut Rivalries look, Ravens go all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 10, led by the Tennessee Titans' Rivalries look.
articles.body:
The NFL regular season has officially passed the halfway point, meaning we are approaching the final chances to see threads on the field. Thankfully, the uniform heat isn't stopping any time soon as alternates continue to make headlines around the league. This week, it's the Tennessee Titans' turn as they debut their Rivalries look.

Tennessee will wear its "Music City"-inspired combination against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It includes a two-tone blue color palette with a Titans-blue lid and navy uniform. The numbers are reminiscent of a neon sign, a nod to those that run through Nashville. "Music City" runs across the chest, while six rhythmic stripes run down the side, similar to strings on a guitar. 

It's a fresh look for the Baltimore Ravens, too, who will debut their all-black combination against the Los Angeles Chargers on "Monday Night Football." The headline for Baltimore's threads is a new matte black lid, nicknamed the "Darkness Helmet." It includes black talon stripes and a two-toned Ravens logo that features red eyes. The shield shoulder patch is black and midnight purple, while "darkness there and nothing more" runs on the inside collar -- a reference to a quote from Edgar Allen Poe's "The Raven."

Monochromatic alternates are popular around the rest of the league. The Cincinnati Bengals will wear their "White Bengal" helmet with all-white uniforms, first introduced in 2022, against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cincinnati has gone 5-1 in the white helmets since they debuted in 2022. The New York Jets are rocking the "Legacy Black" threads against the Buffalo Bills, while the New Orleans Saints will also go all-black against the Carolina Panthers. It's "Alpha Dawg" week for the Cleveland Browns, who will don all-brown against the Houston Texans.

Fans of nostalgia aren't leaving empty-handed. The San Francisco 49ers are wearing their red 1994 throwback threads against the Dallas Cowboys on the road for a classic uniform matchup. Thursday night had the New York Giants rocking their vintage white look against the Washington Commanders for the final time this season.

articles.headline: Borussia Dortmund to end controversial sponsorship with arms manufacturer
articles.description: Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans.
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans as soon as it was signed.

The official sponsorship agreement between the German club and Rheinmetall, which has been in place since 2024, expires on June, 30, 2027.

- Dortmund fans use dummy tank to protest arms-maker deal

Club chairman Carsten Cramer said in an interview published on the club's website Friday that members had voted at the 2024 annual general meeting on a motion not to extend the partnership deal beyond 2027.

"Naturally, we took that into account in our discussions with Rheinmetall and treated it seriously," he said. "We are, of course, aware that our partnership has been controversial from the outset."

When the deal was signed, German media reported it was worth up to €9 million ($10 million) per year.

"From summer 2027, we will lose the income from the sponsorship agreement," Cramer said. "That is a fact. It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."

Rheinmetall is a "champion partner" and Dortmund displays the company's banner on advertising hoardings during games.

The agreement has caused friction among supporters to varying degrees, with some Dortmund fans even going so far as to renounce their support.

Founded in 1889 as "Rheinische Metallwaaren- und Maschinenfabrik Actiengesellschaft," Rheinmetall was one of Germany's biggest armaments manufacturers during both World Wars. It made use of forced labor during World War II.

articles.headline: Ex-lottery pick Doug McDermott retires after 12 NBA seasons
articles.description: Three-point specialist Doug McDermott has retired from the NBA after 12 seasons spent with seven teams.
articles.body:
Doug McDermott announced his retirement Friday after 12 seasons in the NBA.

A first-round pick in the 2014 draft, McDermott carved out a career as a 3-point specialist while playing for seven different teams. In 726 career regular-season games, he averaged 8.5 points, but he shot 41% from beyond the arc, most often in a reserve role.

McDermott, 34, was drafted 11th overall by the Denver Nuggets, but he was traded to the Chicago Bulls on draft night. He spent his first 2½ seasons in Chicago before becoming a journeyman around the league, which included stints with the Oklahoma City Thunder, New York Knicks, Dallas Mavericks, Indiana Pacers and San Antonio Spurs.

He played his last two seasons for the Sacramento Kings from 2024 to 2026, appearing in 71 games during that span.

McDermott burst onto the national scene during his college basketball career where he was a three-time All-American at Creighton, where he played for his father, Greg McDermott, and led the school to four straight NCAA tournament appearances from 2010 to 2014.

He led the nation in scoring in 2013-14, won national player of the year as a senior in 2014 and finished his career with the fifth-most points in NCAA Division I men's basketball history (currently seventh).

Creighton basketball retired his jersey in December 2023.

McDermott's agency, Priority Sports, announced his retirement.

articles.headline: 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!
articles.description: Who is the best soccer player in the world at the November international break? ESPN's latest rankings are here.
articles.body:
For as much as I make fun of the Ballon d'Or process and how ridiculous the mushy, vague, contradictory criteria are, I think they've probably gotten it right in each of the past three years. At least, they haven't gotten it wrong.

When I wrote up my theoretical ballots in each of the past three years, my three choices were Rodri, Ousmane Dembélé and Harry Kane -- the three eventual winners. Once you move beyond the top pick, though, things start to get really weird. Imagine watching the 2025-26 Premier League season and then finding out that Chelsea's Marc Cucurella got more Ballon d'Or votes than Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhães and William Saliba -- combined.

Since the award tends to identify one of the best players on one of the best teams in the world, it does tend to identify a worthy winner. But it rarely identifies any other worthy winners.

Remember when Mohamed Salah led the Premier League in goals and assists two seasons ago for a dominant Liverpool team? He finished fourth, with a vote total closer to 30th than first.

Who, then, is the best player in the world right now? Or rather, who are the best players in the world right now?

In August, we launched the 10 Best List, a recurring look at who I'd estimate to be the -- you got it -- 10 best soccer players in the world. We're back, post-Harry Kane Ballon d'Or, to update the list.

As a reminder, I'm using this as my guidance: "If you added this player to an average round-of-16 Champions League team, how much more likely would the team be to win the tournament?" And if a player is injured or has been injured recently, I'm dropping him out of the top 10.

All right, let's get to the list.

10. Vitinha, midfielder, Paris Saint-Germain

Previous rank: Unranked

Because of the injury rule I made up, we've had to drop Dembélé (No. 1) and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (No. 3) from the list. The former hasn't played since before Halloween, while the latter is out for the season with a torn ACL. And yet it seems like PSG remain the best soccer team in the world without either of them.

Last year, Arsenal finished the league phase of the UEFA Champions League with 23 goals, more than anyone else. PSG currently have 20 goals -- through four Champions League games, two of which were against Manchester City and Barcelona.

So, they have to have someone on the list. I don't think Vitinha would be a controversial pick here for pretty much anyone other than a guy who published a book that devotes an entire chapter to the issues with evaluating, measuring and valuing midfield play. But that guy also happens to be writing this article.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.headline: Barcelona fan for life -- and beyond: Fans can pay to deposit ashes at Camp Nou
articles.description: Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.
articles.body:
Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.

As part of the upgrade to Camp Nou, Barça will have a 1,500m² Memorial space consisting of commemorative plaques and 26,000 niches, where fans' ashes can be deposited.

Both the columbarium and commemorative plaques come with concessions lasting for 10, 25 or 50-year periods. Both options are available to Barça fans worldwide as there is no need to be a club member.

"Two ways of paying tribute and showing remembrance will be available through placing a loved one's ashes in a columbarium or writing a name and message on a commemorative plaque in the Stadium. Both options are available to FC Barcelona fans worldwide, there is no need to be a member," a club statement said.

A peaceful resting place at the Camp Nou will cost from €2,490 ($2,762) for a 10-year concession while the 50-year concession will set you back €5,990 ($6,644). In addition, there is a maintenance fee of €70 per year. A standard 10-year plaque is €490 while a 50-year premium one is €1,040.

Designed by architect Quique Montoya, the Memorial space will combine "fine materials, warm lighting and a contemporary style, with large murals dedicated to notable moments in Barça's history, plus visual, audiovisual and sound elements."

The work, which is being carried out in two phases, will be completed in mid-2028.

"Many fans, members and those with a past at the Club have shown interest in the FC Barcelona Memorial since the launch of the project," the club said.

"These include several former players and relatives of historic figures at Barça who have shown their desire to form part of the initiative."
